from_quote: All legislative powers Herein Granted shall be vested in a congress of the United States.
rationale: Quotes this clause in quotation marks, introduced in the preceding line as what "Sect, first, of the new constitution, says."
to_quote: All legislative Powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States

from_quote: The second section of the federal constitution says, that the members of the house of representatives shall be chosen every second year, and the electors shall have the qualifications requisite for electors of the most numerous branch of the state legislature.
rationale: Cites "The second section" and reproduces this clause, largely in its own words, without quotation marks.
to_quote: The House of Representatives shall be composed of Members chosen every second Year by the People of the several States, and the Electors in each State shall have the Qualifications requisite for Electors of the most numerous Branch of the State Legislature.

from_quote: The second section also says, no person shall be elected a representative who shall not have been seven years an inhabitant of the United States.
rationale: Cites "The second section" for the seven-year requirement for a representative; the clause's words are "seven Years a Citizen," where the essay has "seven years an inhabitant."
to_quote: No Person shall be a Representative who shall not have attained to the Age of twenty five Years, and been seven Years a Citizen of the United States

from_quote: Sect, third, of the new constitution, says, each state shall choose two senators, &c.
rationale: Cites "Sect, third" (OCR comma for a period) for the provision that each state shall choose two senators, which is this clause.

from_quote: The third section further provides, that the senate shall choose their own officers.
rationale: Cites "The third section" for the provision that the senate shall choose its officers, which is this clause.
to_quote: The Senate shall chuse their other Officers

from_quote: The third section also provides, that the senate shall have the sole power to try all impeachments.
rationale: Cites "The third section" and reproduces the first sentence of this clause verbatim.
to_quote: The Senate shall have the sole Power to try all Impeachments.

from_quote: will not have it in their power to try any person, without the consent of two-thirds of the members
rationale: Continues on the impeachment clause cited in Cassius.8.13, naming its requirement of "the consent of two-thirds of the members."
to_quote: no Person shall be convicted without the Concurrence of two thirds of the Members present

from_quote: they can only disqualify him from holding any office of power and trust in the United States: and after that he comes within the jurisdiction of the law of the land.
rationale: Describes the limit of judgment in impeachment to disqualification from office, after which the person is subject to the law, which only this clause provides.
to_quote: disqualification to hold and enjoy any Office of honor, Trust or Profit under the United States

from_quote: is contained in the fourth section, which provides, that the time and place for electing senators and representatives shall be appointed by the different state legislatures, except Congress shall at any time make a law to alter such regulation
rationale: Cites "the fourth section" and paraphrases this clause on the times and places of electing senators and representatives.
to_quote: The Times, Places and Manner of holding Elections for Senators and Representatives, shall be prescribed in each State by the Legislature thereof; but the Congress may at any time by Law make or alter such Regulations

from_quote: must be a greater numbskull than a Vox Populi or an Agrippa,
rationale: Names Agrippa in passing, beside Vox Populi (not in the library), among the "Anti-federal scribblers in the Mass. Gazette" (the author's own note); no one essay is identified, and Agrippa 1 to 6 had appeared by December 14, 1787.
